scope: Read-only Architect review, done in the Architect role. Reviewed caeba9db and a94b41cc (plus 79fa3195, the A2 report the Owner has now approved) on branch codex/r0025-p402-s1 against main a006b039. Files read: the two blueprints (BP-INF-RAIT-CASE-001.json, BP-INF-RAIT-WORKLIST-001.json), the two generated CRUD OpenAPI files (both now have zero paths), the two handwritten *.commands.openapi.json files, P4-02-S1-method-dispositions.json, P4-02-S1-architect-checkpoint.md, P4-02-S1-security-prerequisite.md, AUTHORIZATION.md (S1, the apply.sh extension and A2 are recorded as approved), ADR-0046 and ADR-0047, the closed T0 access map and the T0 triage-field map. I also read the existing rait-case-command.service.ts protocol and claim SQL for context only. Things I confirmed: the six frozen source sha256 values match main a006b039. The 107 methods split as CASE 56 generated + 17 handwritten and WORKLIST 26 generated + 8 handwritten. Dispositions are 71 replaced, 25 retained-scoped and 11 removed. The 11 removed are CASE PATCH, CASE DELETE and nine child DELETEs; parties DELETE is the only child DELETE kept. No method is dropped outside the matrix. No claim-context, risk, legacy-qualification, selector or threshold endpoint was added. All 25 existing command operations and their 4 input schemas are byte-identical to main except one added x-rait-scope annotation each. Every case-bearing read projection (S/O/M/J/T) matches the T0 field tables exactly, with additionalProperties:false and tenant_id excluded. O is correctly absent for parties, documents and admissibility. The T projections match the triage map: no document_number or contact_email on parties, and no filename or content_hash on documents. Generic write inputs match the closed allowlists: parties use the ordinary field set without representation_verified or representation_document_id; document update is filename only; every other resource has an empty set with minProperties 1, so any body returns 400. Document POST has no 2xx response. WORKLIST functional reads are the main DTOs minus tenant_id. batch-items expose only batch_id, case_id and member_id. clock-alerts use id and clock_id. RaitCaseReadScope and RaitCasePoolScope are internal operations[] entities with no public CRUD: active defaults to false, provenance must be nonempty, exactly one unit or pool, the role set follows ADR-0047, and the composite membership FK has precedent in 75-boat-renaest-job.sql. The tenant_id/id FK target indexes exist on rait_case, rait_unit and rait_pool. Defense-only pool uniqueness is relaxed, while JARI/CETRAN uniqueness for unit-bound pools and the unit-null base index are unchanged. WORKLIST depends on CASE, never the reverse. The supporting DDL file 19-rait-case-scope-enforce.sql and the apply.sh edit are described in the checkpoint but not implemented, which is expected. Not done: no edits, generation, runtime, DB, tests or scorecard access. Missing runtime controllers, generated clients and RED tests are expected at this checkpoint and are not counted as findings.

findings.problem: removeRaitParty (DELETE /v1/inf/rait/parties/{id}) is the only child DELETE kept, and its contract promises a 200 success. But it is limited to the 'existing technical-admin action and independently complete case purpose'. Under the T0 role table, technical-admin gets functional projections only and is denied on generic CASE routes, and T0 forbids combining one role's permission with another role's scope. So no principal can ever reach the 200, which breaks the S1 rule that retained positive paths must succeed. The checkpoint also says T0 requires an independently sourced ordinary-metadata contract before a DELETE is kept, but it cites no such source for parties. This conflict sits inside T0 itself (the retained-write matrix versus the role table); the source copies it faithfully.
findings.recommendation: Do not change the approved 71/25/11 counts or the ADRs. Before Inspector GREEN, add an Architect note to the S1 reports naming either the sourced owner contract and reachable role/purpose for party DELETE, or an explicit statement that no principal satisfies it in S1. In the second case Inspector asserts the denial (403 or scoped 404) and no positive, instead of expecting a 200 that can never happen.

findings.problem: The supporting-DDL text describes the pool-link triggers as plain equality, case.unit_id=pool.unit_id. rait_case.unit_id is nullable, and the unit-null base pools (ux_inf_rait_pool_instance) are kept on purpose. Existing protocol and claim SQL compares with 'is not distinct from'. Plain SQL equality evaluates to NULL for unit-null cases and pools, so a trigger written from this text would reject, or silently fail to validate, every link between a unit-null case and its base pool.
findings.recommendation: Clarify in the S1 report that the compatibility check in 19-rait-case-scope-enforce.sql uses null-safe equality (IS NOT DISTINCT FROM) for unit_id plus strict instance equality, matching the existing command SQL. Have Inspector cover both a unit-null base pool and a unit-bound pool.

findings.problem: Version 1.5.1 lets a unit hold more than one same-unit defesa_previa pool in S1, but the code paths that assume one pool per unit/instance stay as they are until S2. Protocol requires exactly one active secretaria membership matching instance+unit and fails with 403 otherwise (rait-case-command.service.ts ~L626-646). claim-next picks candidates by instance plus unit (is not distinct from) with no exact-pool containment. A secretary placed in two same-unit defense pools would therefore lose a legal protocol, and an analyst in a second pool could claim cases routed to the first. Nothing is provisioned now, so this is latent, but the checkpoint says only that legal success is unchanged and does not name these dependencies.
findings.recommendation: Record in the S1 report a binding interim condition: no second same-unit defense pool may be provisioned, even in operational fixtures meant to show functional parity, until S2 brings claim-next under exact-pool containment. Engineer must make sure the protocol membership resolver cannot regress to 403 once more than one pool matches. Inspector should cover this alongside the same-unit defense-pool exclusion test the checkpoint already requires.

findings.problem: Read responses are untagged anyOf unions of the S/O/M/J/T projections, and the T0 field subsets overlap (for example S is a subset of M for most resources). A client or validator therefore cannot tell from the response which purpose projection a row is. A multi-role list could contain rows under different projections with nothing marking them, which makes the T0 rule against silently mixing AUDITOR S with M rows hard to see from the contract. This does not misstate any field (A2 approved omission-aware consumers, and projections are not cast to full DTOs), but it limits how much the contract alone can show.
findings.recommendation: Optionally document in x-rait-scope that each row is exactly one server-chosen projection and that one response never mixes S and M for the same purpose. Have Inspector check field sets per row by role. If a discriminator is wanted later, propose it as a separate contract change rather than adding it to S1.

findings.problem: The unique indexes on rait_case_read_scope (tenant, actor, role, unit or pool) apply to inactive rows too, and the entity has no revocation provenance (no revoked_at, revoked_by or revocation_ref). Re-granting after a revocation therefore means reactivating the old row in place and overwriting authorization_ref, which loses the provenance history ADR-0046/0047 expect ('verified provisioning provenance... revocation'). rait_case_pool_scope's unique (tenant, case, pool) is required by ADR-0047, so that table is out of scope for this finding.
findings.recommendation: Not blocking for S1, since no public write API or provisioning exists. Record that the internal writer must keep an append-only audit of activation and revocation, or propose later a partial unique index WHERE active plus revocation fields. Do not change the ADRs.

findings.problem: listRaitClockAlert accepts case_id and pool_id filters but not clock_id, even though T0 makes clock_id the common identifier and the parent link for clock-alerts (alert→clock→case). This only affects how convenient filtering is; filters never grant authority.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add a clock_id filter, or note that the case_id filter is resolved through the clock join. The complete case predicate must still be applied in SQL before pagination.
